leading_positions.synthesis: Four members name B056 (targeted protein degradation) with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. They share the view that the PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies) and the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide-type glues (Handa) are two datable discoveries that fit one citation about recruiting E3 ligases to remove chosen proteins. Aili and Chabes would accept Ciulli as third name only if the committee wants a PROTAC-centred citation; Brzezinski asks that the expert report show how much of the ternary-complex framework is attributable to Ciulli and not shared with Crews. Aqvist moved from Ciulli to Handa after reading Aili's opening. Aili and Chabes would not split B056 into separate PROTAC and glue parts unless no unified citation can be agreed. Shared caveats are that no degrader is yet a broadly approved therapy and that Sakamoto, Ito, Gray and Kim are left out.

Three members name B056 with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, valuing Ciulli's structural and biophysical work on VHL ligands and ternary-complex cooperativity as what made degraders drug-like and quantitatively understood. Their citations differ in whether the glue strand is named: Linke's wording covers bifunctional molecules only but he would add 'induced proximity to ubiquitin ligases' so both strands fit, and Sparr's and Zou's wordings mention glue-type or molecular-glue molecules even though Handa and Ito are not among the three names. Sparr and Zou say they would accept Handa if the committee chooses him; Linke says he can be persuaded that cereblon was the more decisive original step. Zou notes that taking Handa would displace Ciulli, and the Aili camp would not give up Handa. Together with the first group, seven of eight members prefer B056 as the ballot, but no single trio of laureates yet has five votes (four for Crews, Deshaies, Handa; three for Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli).

Somfai alone prefers B051 (Pd-catalysed C-N coupling) with Buchwald and Hartwig, citing a mature, widely adopted general method with a clean two-person credit split. He lists B056 and B017 as alternatives and says he would move toward B056 if the committee wants to reward a modality rather than a method. His main stated vulnerabilities are the overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize and Kosugi's precedent.

areas_of_agreement: Seven of eight members place B056 in their preferred configuration; only Somfai (B051) does not, and he lists B056 as his first alternative.

All eight round-1 files describe the same chemical principle for B056: recruitment of an E3 ligase into a ternary complex giving event-driven, catalytic removal of a target, with independently reproduced mechanism across laboratories.
Crews and Deshaies are named by all seven B056 supporters as the core of any B056 citation, for the PROTAC concept and first proof of principle.

Members who comment on B024 (phase separation) consistently regard it as a candidate for a later year because in vivo functional relevance remains contested, and Sparr, who ranked it first in the opening, acknowledges that caveat herself.
Members who comment on B060 (nitrogenase) accept its scientific merit but regard the catalytic cycle as unsettled and the credit among five names as hard to divide.
Several members say the B056 citation should rest on the chemical and mechanistic principle and not on therapeutic outcomes.
scientific_disputes: Whether the third B056 laureate should be Ciulli, whose VHL ligands and ternary-complex cooperativity are presented as the quantitative design basis, or Handa, whose cereblon discovery is presented as the mechanistic anchor of the glue strand and of most clinical degraders; supporters of each side describe the other's contribution as enabling or as a single family of molecules rather than a founding step.

Whether PROTACs and cereblon-based molecular glues are one achievement (induced proximity to E3 ligases) or two lineages that a single citation would blur; Somfai also doubts how much is chemically new, describing much of the work as ligand and linker optimisation around existing biology.
Whether C-N coupling (B051) is as distinct from the 2010 C-C cross-coupling prize as Suzuki is from Heck (Somfai's view) or an extension of an honoured idea (Sparr, Zou, Linke, Aqvist raise this).

Whether B059 (molecular-sieve catalysts) contains one sharply defined discovery; Aili, Brzezinski, Linke and Somfai say they cannot identify it, while Zou, who ranked it first in the opening, describes it as structure-determines-function with crystallographically verified designs and broad industrial reach.

Whether perovskite solar absorbers (B068, an alternative for Linke and Zou) are limited by chemistry or by device engineering: Zou says defect and structural chemistry is not in doubt while stability and lead toxicity are engineering issues, whereas Somfai calls them premature as a chemistry award.
attribution_disputes: B056 third seat: Handa (Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Chabes) versus Ciulli (Linke, Sparr, Zou), with explicit willingness to switch on both sides.

Whether Sakamoto (co-author of the 2001 PROTAC paper), Ito (cereblon with Handa), Gray or Kim should displace or share any seat; Brzezinski, Linke and Zou raise Sakamoto, and Sparr, Zou and Somfai raise Ito or Gray.
How much of the ternary-complex and VHL-ligand framework belongs to Ciulli and how much to the Crews laboratory, which Brzezinski wants the expert report to state.

For B051, how much weight Kosugi's tin-amide precedent carries against Buchwald and Hartwig as originators of the general catalytic method (Somfai calls it a precursor; others see residual priority discomfort).

For B048, Aili and Aqvist favour a Liu-only citation because Komor and Gaudelli were Liu trainees and Nishida and Kondo's parallel work is a separate claim; B048 is only an alternative for Aili, Aqvist, Chabes and Linke, so this is not a configuration in any member's preferred prize.

For B060, B024, B059 and B017, members point to unresolved splits among five candidates each (Rees, Einsle, Seefeldt, Dean, Ribbe; Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu, Mittag; Corma, Davis, Zones and others; Schultz, Chin, Wang).
maturity_disputes: No degrader is yet a broadly established approved therapy; Aqvist, Brzezinski, Chabes, Linke, Sparr, Zou and Aili all note this. Sparr argues that waiting for an approved drug would hold the prize hostage to regulatory events and that twenty-five years of independent reproduction is the relevant maturity, while Chabes and Linke say they are recalling trial status and not verifying it.
B024: whether condensates are functionally phase-separated in vivo or in vitro demixing; Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Chabes, Linke, Somfai and Zou each say this makes it premature for this year.
B060: substrate-binding state and catalytic cycle still debated (Aqvist, Chabes, Somfai, Sparr, Zou); Brzezinski himself concedes the cycle is not closed.
B048: proximity to the 2020 CRISPR prize is raised by Aili, Aqvist and Linke; B052: overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize is raised by Sparr.
B051: how much the 2010 prize reduces the case, which Somfai says need not be a bar, and which Aqvist, Linke, Sparr and Zou treat as a real obstacle.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Zou works on zeolites and porous frameworks and flags professional familiarity with Jihong Yu and Michael Tsapatsis (B059); she says she would recuse from deciding on B059 if it advances.

Brzezinski flags a Stockholm University colleague relationship with Zou, who ranked B059 first, as a possible perceived connection and not a recusal issue; Zou states the same relationship with Brzezinski and says it is not a conflict.
Aqvist reports having served on the committee with Brzezinski since 2015 and describes this as a committee relationship, not a conflict.
Sparr's research on lipid self-assembly and membranes is close to B052 (ionizable lipid nanoparticles), an alternative she lists; she knows of no tie to any credited candidate.

Linke (chair), Somfai and Sparr are Lund colleagues, and Aili's research overlaps scientifically with Sparr's; both are described as collegial or scientific connections with no tie to any shortlisted candidate.
No member reports a personal, mentoring or institutional tie to any credited name on B056 or B051.
questions_for_round2: For the third B056 seat, does the committee prefer Handa or Ciulli, and what evidence from the expert reports on priority and on how much of the VHL and ternary-complex framework is distinct from the Crews laboratory would settle it?

Can a single citation, for example one about recruiting ubiquitin ligases to remove chosen proteins, be worded to cover both PROTACs and cereblon-based glues without naming all contributors, and does a Ciulli-based trio leave the glue strand unrecognised in an acceptable way?
If the committee prefers a different third name, do Sakamoto (2001 co-author), Ito or Gray have a claim strong enough to displace Crews, Deshaies or the third seat, and on what dated discovery?

Does the absence of a broadly approved degrader make B056 premature, and if not, what criterion for demonstrated impact should the citation rest on, given that several members say it should rest on the chemistry?
Somfai: what distinguishes the original C-N coupling advance from Kosugi's precedent and from the 2010 prize, and can it stand alone as a citation if the committee prefers a method prize?

If B056 does not secure five votes for one trio, which alternative (B048 with Liu alone or with trainees, B052, B017, B068 or B051) does the committee prefer as a second part, and who would be the laureates and the citation?
Brzezinski: has any mechanistic result settled the substrate-binding state of nitrogenase, and can B060 be credited to a single step if it is reconsidered?
summary.chair_observation: The first round shows broad convergence on B056 as a topic, with seven of eight members preferring it, but divergence on the third laureate: four members favour Handa and three favour Ciulli, and each side states it could accept the other. No configuration has a majority of five on its own. Somfai's B051 is the only preferred ballot outside B056, and B048, B052, B068 and B017 appear as alternatives for two to four members each. Several members' responses refer to earlier-stage positions (for example Aqvist's third seat, which moved from Ciulli to Handa), so round 2 should work from the current round-1 configurations.
